news.title: Ten Months In: How Ngoma Charts' Top 50 Has Actually Shifted
news.excerpt: Since launch, Kenya has overtaken Tanzania as the single largest source of Singles Top 50 entries, even as the Albums chart has stayed dominated by acts from outside East Africa. A ten-month data check-in.
news.body:
Ngoma Charts closed its tenth monthly cycle this week, and the accumulated data shows real movement beneath the month-to-month headlines. In September 2025, the chart's first Singles Top 50 was led by Tanzania with 17 entries to Kenya's 13. By June 2026, that order had flipped: Kenya placed 16 songs in the Top 50 to Tanzania's 15 — a two-country race that has stayed close for ten straight months but has now changed leaders.

The Albums chart tells a different story. Its June 2026 Top 50 is led by the United States with nine entries, followed by Nigeria, Canada, and Kenya tied at seven apiece — a far more globally distributed table than the Singles chart, where East Africa alone has consistently accounted for roughly three of every five entries.

Across both charts, 44 releases have now earned Gold or Platinum certification, seven of them Platinum. And of the ten monthly #1 singles crowned so far, five have come from Kenya, two from Tanzania, and one each from Uganda, the United States, and Jamaica — five different countries in ten months, with East Africa still holding the majority.

Ten months is a small sample for a chart tracking six platforms and dozens of countries. But the shift from a Tanzania-led Top 50 to a Kenya-led one is the first real trend line Ngoma Charts' data has produced — and it's the one worth watching heading into month eleven.

news.title: Second Certification Round: 'Donjo Maber' and 'Taya' Upgrade to Platinum
news.excerpt: A second certification round upgrades Iyanii & Dufla's 'Donjo Maber' and Okello Max's 'Taya' to Platinum, while Bien's 'Alusa Why Are You Topless?' and Gunna's 'One of Wun' earn the same honor on the Albums side.
news.body:
Ngoma's second certification round has landed, and it belongs to the chart's earliest hits. Iyanii & Dufla's "Donjo Maber" — the very first #1 in the chart's history — and Okello Max's "Taya" both upgrade from Gold to Platinum, joined by Bien's "Alusa Why Are You Topless?" and Gunna's "One of Wun" on the Albums side.

Collo Blue & ADDEH PRINCE's "Up Burukanga" earns a fresh Gold certification from Kenya, while Don Toliver's "OCTANE" and Zuchu's "Peace and Money" add new Gold awards on the Albums chart.

Two certification rounds in, a clear pattern is emerging: the releases earning the biggest honors are the ones with the longest chart histories, not necessarily the ones currently sitting at #1.
news.author: Certifications Desk

news.title: Asake Holds Albums #1 for a Second Month as Drake Debuts at #3
news.excerpt: Asake's 'M$NEY' holds #1 for a second straight month on Ngoma's Albums chart, while South Africa's JAZZWRLD & Thukuthela climb ten places to #2 and Drake's 'ICEMAN' makes its first chart appearance at #3.
news.body:
Asake's "M$NEY" holds #1 on Ngoma's Albums chart for a second consecutive month, though its points total drops sharply to 592 — a reminder that even chart-topping albums lose momentum as they age past their debut window.

JAZZWRLD & Thukuthela's "The Most Wanted" is the month's biggest mover, climbing ten places to #2 (506 points), South Africa's strongest Albums chart showing to date. Drake makes his first appearance on Ngoma's Albums chart as "ICEMAN" debuts at #3 (475 points).

With ten months of data now on record, Ngoma's Albums chart has been led by acts from four different countries — the United States, Nigeria (twice), and Kenya — a wider spread than the Singles chart's five leaders, four of which have come from Kenya or Tanzania.
news.author: Ngoma Charts Newsroom

news.title: 'Finale' Extends Its #1 Run to Three Months, a New Ngoma Charts Record
news.excerpt: Bien & Alikiba's 'Finale' holds #1 for a third consecutive month, the longest Singles-chart reign since Ngoma Charts launched, as Mbosso returns to the top five with a new single, 'Ozalima.'
news.body:
Bien & Alikiba's "Finale" closes June still at #1, its third consecutive month on top and the longest run any single has had on Ngoma Charts' Singles chart, surpassing "Donjo Maber" and "Pawa," which each managed two months before being dethroned.

Mbosso opens a new front in the chart with "Ozalima," debuting at #2 — even as his earlier hit "Pawa" climbs two places to #5, marking the first time Mbosso has held two separate entries in the same published top five. Ywaya Tajiri's "Chai ya saa kumi" holds at #3, and Toxic Lyrikali's "Hate" climbs seven places to #4, his second top-five single after "Backbencher" in the chart's opening months.

Ten months into Ngoma Charts' run, "Finale" has now set the Singles-chart standard for longevity. On the Albums side, that record still belongs to Cardi B, at four months.

news.title: Ngoma Charts Awards Its First Gold and Platinum Certifications
news.excerpt: Nine months of chart data have produced Ngoma's first certification wave: 35 Gold awards and two immediate Platinum upgrades, led by Mbosso's 'Pawa' and Joshua Baraka & JAE5's 'Wrong Places.'
news.body:
Ngoma Charts has issued its first round of certifications, awarding Gold to 35 releases that crossed the platform's points threshold across their chart run, with two of them — Mbosso's "Pawa" (482 points) and Joshua Baraka & JAE5's "Wrong Places" (418 points) — certified Platinum outright.

The wave spans both charts and multiple countries: Iyanii & Dufla's "Donjo Maber" (420 points) and Okello Max's "Taya" (433 points) both go Gold from Kenya, alongside Gunna's "The Last Wun" (460 points), which goes Platinum on the Albums side. Burna Boy's "No Sign of Weakness," Bien's "Alusa Why Are You Topless?," Cardi B's "AM I THE DRAMA? (Ultimate Edition)," and Asake's "Lungu Boy" are among the album certifications, alongside regional entries from South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, and Nigeria.

With certification points accumulating separately from monthly rank, several releases that have since fallen out of the published top five — including some from the chart's earliest months — qualify for recognition their current chart position no longer reflects.

news.title: Ywaya Tajiri's 17-Place Jump Ties for the Chart's Second-Biggest Move
news.excerpt: 'Chai ya saa kumi' rose from #19 to #2 in a single month — a jump matched only by 'Mfisadi' in April, and second only to Gradine Toto's record 41-place leap in March.
news.body:
Ywaya Tajiri's "Chai ya saa kumi" climbed from #19 to #2 in May, a 17-place jump that ties Toxic Lyrikali & Dyana Cods' "Mfisadi" (April, #21 to #4) for the second-biggest single-month move in Ngoma Charts history — behind only Gradine Toto's record-setting 41-place leap in March.

Big jumps are becoming a regular feature of the Singles chart rather than a rarity: four of the chart's first nine months have now produced a move of at least 13 places somewhere in the published top five, and two of those have arrived in the last two months alone.

Whether that reflects genuinely fast-breaking songs or simply a deeper, more competitive pool of releases each month, the trend is now well-established enough to watch for every month going forward.
news.author: Data & Analytics Desk

news.title: Asake's 'M$NEY' Debuts at #1, Ending Bien's One-Month Stay at the Top
news.excerpt: Asake's 'M$NEY' enters Ngoma's Albums chart directly at #1, moving Bien's 'Alusa Why Are You Topless?' out of the top three entirely after just one month leading the chart.
news.body:
Asake's "M$NEY" debuts at #1 on Ngoma's Albums chart with 1,197 points, Nigeria's first #1 album since the chart's early months. The debut is notable for what it displaces: Bien's "Alusa Why Are You Topless?," which reached #1 in April after five months of trying, drops out of the published top three entirely after just a single month on top.

Cardi B's "AM I THE DRAMA? (Ultimate Edition)" holds steady at #2 with 1,146 points, still a fixture in the top three eight months into the chart's run despite no longer leading it. Bridget Blue's "RNB" holds at #3 for a second straight month, matching its April position exactly.

Nine months in, Ngoma's Albums #1 has now changed hands six times — never held by the same act in back-to-back cycles for longer than Cardi B's four-month run.
news.author: Ngoma Charts Newsroom

news.title: 'Finale' Holds #1 for a Second Month as Rwanda Debuts in the Top Five
news.excerpt: Bien & Alikiba's 'Finale' stays at #1 for a second straight month, while Rwanda earns its first-ever Singles top-five entry via 'AYAYAAH,' a three-way collaboration featuring Bien for a second month running.
news.body:
Bien & Alikiba's "Finale" holds #1 for a second consecutive month, closing May with 1,404 points. Ywaya Tajiri's "Chai ya saa kumi" is the month's biggest riser, jumping 17 places to #2.

Rwanda records its first-ever Singles top-five appearance as "AYAYAAH," a collaboration between ELEMENT EleéeH, Joshua Baraka, and Bien, debuts at #3. It's Bien's second straight month connected to a top-five single beyond his own name-brand release. Wakadinali's "LAST DANCE" enters at #4, while Mejja & Fik Fameica's "Siaka" falls three places to #5 after a month at #2.

With four of the month's top five singles either new or climbing sharply, May is shaping up as one of the chart's more competitive months for the #2 through #5 positions.
news.author: Ngoma Charts Newsroom

news.title: Bien's April: A Single at #1, an Album at #1, and a Feature in the Top Five
news.excerpt: Between 'Finale,' 'Alusa Why Are You Topless?,' and a guest feature, Bien is connected to three of Ngoma's top charting releases this month — a first for any artist since launch.
news.body:
No artist has had a month on Ngoma Charts quite like Bien's April. "Finale," his duet with Alikiba, opens at #1 on the Singles chart. "Alusa Why Are You Topless?," his own album, reaches #1 on the Albums chart for the first time after five months of trying. And credits aside, Bien has now appeared on charting releases in three of Ngoma's first eight months.

Reaching #1 on both charts in the same month, as one artist, hasn't happened before on Ngoma Charts — every prior Singles and Albums #1 has belonged to different acts. Whether that becomes a repeatable feat or an April one-off is a question only the coming months can answer.

For now, the data has a clear answer to who had the biggest month: Bien did.
news.author: Artist Desk

news.title: Bien's 'Alusa' Finally Reaches #1, Ending Cardi B's Four-Month Reign
news.excerpt: After five months parked in the Albums top three, Bien's 'Alusa Why Are You Topless?' climbs to #1, ending 'AM I THE DRAMA? (Ultimate Edition)'s four-month hold on the top spot.
news.body:
It took five months, but Bien's "Alusa Why Are You Topless?" finally reaches #1 on Ngoma's Albums chart, climbing one place to 1,359 points. It's the album's first time at the top after spending every prior month at #2 or #3 — and it ends Cardi B's four-month reign at #1, the longest in the chart's history.

"AM I THE DRAMA? (Ultimate Edition)" drops to #2 with 1,190 points, still comfortably inside the top three even in defeat. Bridget Blue's "RNB" debuts at #3 with 1,172 points, Kenya's second album in the Albums top three this month alongside Bien's.

With Bien now leading the Albums chart the same month "Finale" leads the Singles chart, April marks the first time one artist has been connected to #1 on both Ngoma charts simultaneously.
news.author: Ngoma Charts Newsroom

news.title: Bien & Alikiba's 'Finale' Debuts at #1 as Kenya Claims Both Top Two Singles Spots
news.excerpt: 'Finale' opens at #1 on Ngoma's Singles chart, with Mejja & Fik Fameica's 'Siaka' entering right behind it at #2 — the first time one country has held both of the chart's top two positions.
news.body:
Bien & Alikiba's "Finale" enters Ngoma's Singles chart directly at #1 with 1,593 points, returning Kenya to the top spot for the first time since "Donjo Maber's" run ended in November. Mejja & Fik Fameica's "Siaka" debuts right behind it at #2 (1,101 points) — the first time Kenya has held both of the chart's top two positions at once.

Mbosso's "Pawa" slips one place to #3, still the only single to have spent time at #1 in three separate months. Toxic Lyrikali & Dyana Cods' "Mfisadi" jumps 17 places to #4, while Vybz Kartel & Shenseea's "Panic" falls four spots to #5 after a month at #1 in March.

With two new Kenyan entries running 1-2 and last month's chart-topper already dropped to #5, April's table is Ngoma's fastest-moving yet.
news.author: Ngoma Charts Newsroom

news.title: Who Is Gradine Toto? The Story Behind Ngoma's Biggest Chart Jump
news.excerpt: 'MAYDAY RACHAEL' went from barely charting to the Singles Top 3 in a single month. A look at the record-breaking climb, by the numbers.
news.body:
A month ago, Gradine Toto's "MAYDAY RACHAEL" sat at #44 on Ngoma's Singles chart — one of the last songs to make the cut. This month, it sits at #3, a 41-place climb that stands alone as the largest single-month jump the chart has recorded.

For context: the previous record was 13 places (Dave & Tems' "Raindance," in January), and only one other release — Marioo's "The Godson," at six places — had cracked double digits at all. "MAYDAY RACHAEL's" jump isn't just bigger than those moves. It's more than three times the previous record.

Six months of chart history is still a short baseline, but if there's a lesson so far, it's this: on Ngoma Charts, a song sitting quietly in the 40s can be one strong month away from the Top 5.
news.author: Artist Desk

news.title: Cardi B Ties the Record With a Fourth Straight Month at Albums #1
news.excerpt: 'AM I THE DRAMA? (Ultimate Edition)' holds #1 for a fourth consecutive month, the longest reign in Ngoma Charts' six-month history, as Bien's 'Alusa' returns to #2.
news.body:
Cardi B's "AM I THE DRAMA? (Ultimate Edition)" holds #1 on the Albums chart for a fourth straight month, closing March with 1,430 points — no release, on either the Singles or Albums chart, has led for this long since Ngoma Charts launched six months ago.

Bien's "Alusa Why Are You Topless?" climbs back to #2 with 1,365 points, its fifth month in the Albums top three. Brent Faiyaz's "Icon (Director's Cut)" provides the month's biggest mover, jumping 16 places to #3 — a number that would have led the headlines in any month before Gradine Toto's 41-place surge on the Singles chart this same month.

Four months at #1 is now the number every future Albums chart-topper will be measured against.
news.author: Data & Analytics Desk

news.title: Vybz Kartel & Shenseea's 'Panic' Debuts at #1 as Gradine Toto Leaps 41 Places
news.excerpt: Jamaica claims its first Ngoma Charts #1 as 'Panic' debuts at the top, while Gradine Toto's 'MAYDAY RACHAEL' produces the biggest single-month jump the chart has ever recorded, rising 41 places to #3.
news.body:
Vybz Kartel & Shenseea's "Panic" enters Ngoma Charts' Singles chart directly at #1 with 1,135 points, Jamaica's first #1 since launch and the third country to top the chart in three consecutive months.

The month's real story sits one place lower. Gradine Toto's "MAYDAY RACHAEL" rises from #44 to #3 — a 41-place jump that shatters the previous record (Dave & Tems' 13-place leap in January) by a wide margin. Mbosso's "Pawa" climbs one spot to #2, while Lil Uzi Vert's "What You Saying" and Joshua Baraka & JAE5's "Wrong Places" each slide down to #4 and #5.

Three different countries have now produced a #1 in three straight months — Jamaica following the United States and, before that, a run of East African leaders. "MAYDAY RACHAEL's" jump, meanwhile, is a new benchmark for how fast a release can move.
news.author: Ngoma Charts Newsroom

news.title: Six Months, Never Below #5: Okello Max's Quiet Consistency
news.excerpt: While the top of the Singles chart has changed hands five times, Okello Max's 'Taya' has stayed inside the top five every single month since Ngoma Charts launched.
news.body:
Five different songs have held #1 on Ngoma's Singles chart since launch. Only one release has been in the top five every single month through all of them: Okello Max's "Taya," which closed February at #5 for its sixth consecutive top-five finish.

"Taya" has never topped the chart, but it has also never left the upper tier — a level of consistency none of the chart's five #1s can claim, since each of them has spent at least one month outside the top three since their peak.

It's a reminder that the chart's biggest headlines aren't always where the most durable performances are happening.
news.author: Artist Desk

news.title: Cardi B's Album Extends Its Run to Three Months at #1
news.excerpt: 'AM I THE DRAMA? (Ultimate Edition)' holds #1 for a third straight month as Don Toliver's 'OCTANE' debuts at #2 and Bien's 'Alusa' settles into a familiar #3.
news.body:
Cardi B's grip on the Albums chart tightens: "AM I THE DRAMA? (Ultimate Edition)" holds #1 for a third consecutive month, posting 1,773 points — no other album has led the chart more than two months running.

Don Toliver's "OCTANE" enters at #2 with 1,665 points, the month's only new arrival in the top three. Bien's "Alusa Why Are You Topless?" slips one place to #3 (1,638 points), a familiar position for a project that has now spent four straight months in the Albums top three without ever reaching #1 itself.

With three months at #1 and counting, Cardi B is closing in on uncharted territory for Ngoma's Albums chart.
news.author: Ngoma Charts Newsroom

news.title: Lil Uzi Vert's 'What You Saying' Becomes Ngoma Charts' First Non-East-African #1
news.excerpt: 'What You Saying' climbs four places to #1, making Lil Uzi Vert the first act from outside East Africa to top Ngoma's Singles chart since it launched five months ago.
news.body:
Every #1 single on Ngoma Charts to date has come from East Africa — until now. Lil Uzi Vert's "What You Saying" climbs four places to #1 with 1,626 points, the first non-East-African single to top the chart since launch.

Tanzania answers immediately with a new entry of its own: D Voice & Zuchu's "Baridi" debuts at #2 with 1,466 points. Mbosso's "Pawa" slips one place to #3, while Joshua Baraka & JAE5's "Wrong Places" falls three spots to #4 after a month at #1 in January. Okello Max's "Taya" holds inside the top five for a sixth straight month at #5.

The five previous #1s were Kenyan or Tanzanian. Whether "What You Saying's" run at the top is a one-month outlier or the start of wider competition for the chart's top spot is the question February leaves behind.
news.author: Ngoma Charts Newsroom

news.title: Raindance's 13-Place Leap: How Big Is Big on Ngoma Charts?
news.excerpt: Dave & Tems' 'Raindance' didn't climb the Singles chart so much as vault it — from #16 to #3 in a single month. Here's how that stacks up against every jump recorded so far.
news.body:
Until January, the biggest move recorded on Ngoma Charts' Singles chart was "Wrong Places'" three-place climb in December. Dave & Tems' "Raindance" reset the bar entirely, rising from #16 to #3 — a 13-place jump in one monthly cycle.

Big single-month jumps tend to mean one of two things: a release picking up meaningfully more six-platform performance than the month before, or a release that was under-tracked early and is catching up to its real audience. Either way, "Raindance" is now the standard other big movers will be measured against.

On the Albums side, Marioo's six-place jump with "The Godson" this same month would have been the headline in any other month. In January, it was the second-biggest story.
news.author: Data & Analytics Desk

news.title: Cardi B Opens 2026 Still at #1; Marioo's 'The Godson' Jumps Six Places
news.excerpt: Cardi B's 'AM I THE DRAMA? (Ultimate Edition)' holds #1 into the new year, while Bien's 'Alusa' returns to #2 and Marioo's 'The Godson' climbs six places into the Albums top three.
news.body:
Cardi B's "Ultimate Edition" continues its run at #1 into 2026, gaining points month over month to 1,904 as it heads into its second month atop the Albums chart. Bien's "Alusa Why Are You Topless?" climbs back to #2 with 1,664 points, its fourth month inside the Albums top three since debuting in November.

Marioo's "The Godson" provides the month's biggest album move, climbing six places to #3 with 1,561 points — Tanzania's strongest Albums chart showing since "Pawa" first put the country at the top of the Singles table.

Four months into 2026's chart cycle, Cardi B remains the only act to have led the Albums chart more than once.
news.author: Ngoma Charts Newsroom

news.title: Joshua Baraka & JAE5's 'Wrong Places' Takes #1 as Dave & Tems Rocket 13 Places
news.excerpt: 'Wrong Places' claims Ngoma Charts' first #1 of 2026, dethroning 'Pawa' after two months, while Dave & Tems' 'Raindance' leaps from #16 to #3 — the biggest jump yet recorded.
news.body:
2026 opens with a new #1: Joshua Baraka & JAE5's "Wrong Places" climbs two places to the top with 1,597 points, ending Mbosso's two-month run at #1. "Pawa" holds at #2 with 1,577 points, a gap of just 20 points between the chart's top two.

The month's headline move belongs to Dave & Tems: "Raindance" rockets from #16 to #3, a 13-place jump that's the largest since Bien's four-place climb in November. Okello Max's "Taya" holds at #4 for a second straight month, while Lil Uzi Vert's "What You Saying" enters at #5 — the chart's first new American entry in the Singles top five since Cardi B's albums began appearing in the Top 3.

Between a new #1, a record jump, and a high-profile debut, January is Ngoma Charts' most eventful month yet.
news.author: Ngoma Charts Newsroom

news.title: Cardi B Returns to #1 With 'Ultimate Edition' as Joshua Baraka Debuts at #2
news.excerpt: A new edition of Cardi B's 'AM I THE DRAMA?' opens at #1 on Ngoma's year-end Albums chart, while Joshua Baraka's debut album 'Juvie' enters directly at #2.
news.body:
Cardi B is back on top of Ngoma's Albums chart, as the "Ultimate Edition" of "AM I THE DRAMA?" opens at #1 with 1,176 points — a new release entry distinct from the "ErrTime Edition" that led the chart in October.

Joshua Baraka's "Juvie" debuts at #2 with 1,160 points, arriving one month after his feature on "Wrong Places" pushed into the Singles top three. Bien's "Alusa Why Are You Topless?" slips one place to #3 (1,158 points), its third straight month in the Albums top three.

With three different editions of Cardi B's album now having appeared across the chart's first four months, the Albums table closes 2025 with its most crowded top three yet — separated by just 18 points.
news.author: Ngoma Charts Newsroom

news.title: 'Pawa' Holds #1 as 2025 Closes; Joshua Baraka & JAE5 Surge to #3
news.excerpt: Mbosso's 'Pawa' closes out 2025 still at #1 on Ngoma Charts, while Joshua Baraka & JAE5's 'Wrong Places' jumps three places to #3 in the year's final Singles chart.
news.body:
Mbosso's "Pawa" ends the year the way it started its reign — at #1, holding steady with 1,411 points as Ngoma Charts closes its fourth monthly cycle. Iyanii & Dufla's "Donjo Maber" stays at #2 (1,365 points), keeping the top two unchanged from November.

The bigger move belongs to Joshua Baraka & JAE5's "Wrong Places," which climbs three places to #3 with 1,264 points, its best showing yet. Okello Max's "Taya" holds at #4, while Ayra Starr & Rema's "Who's Dat Girl" slips two spots to #5 as its debut-month surge cools.

Four months in, Ngoma Charts heads into 2026 with "Pawa" still unbeaten since November — and "Wrong Places" looking like the chart's next serious threat to the top spot.
news.author: Ngoma Charts Newsroom

news.title: Coming in 2026: Ngoma Charts' Certification Program
news.excerpt: Starting next year, releases that cross defined points thresholds on Ngoma Charts will be eligible for Gold and Platinum certification — a new layer of recognition built directly from each release's chart history.
news.body:
As Ngoma Charts closes its first four months, certifications are next. Beginning in 2026, any release that accumulates enough combined points across its chart run becomes eligible for Gold certification; sustained performance beyond that threshold earns Platinum.

Unlike the monthly chart, which resets and re-ranks every cycle, certification points accumulate over a release's full run — rewarding songs and albums that stay on the chart for months, not just the ones that debut highest.

With four monthly cycles of data already in hand and several releases already deep into extended chart runs, the first certifications are expected within the first half of 2026.
news.author: Ngoma Charts Team

news.title: Bien's +4 Jump Is the Biggest Move Ngoma's Albums Chart Has Seen
news.excerpt: 'Alusa Why Are You Topless?' didn't just enter the Albums Top 3 — Bien's project jumped four places to get there, the largest single-month climb recorded since the chart's launch.
news.body:
Movement is normally measured in one or two places. Bien's "Alusa Why Are You Topless?" moved four, climbing from #6 to #2 on Ngoma's November Albums chart — the biggest jump the two-month-old chart has recorded.

The size of the jump matters less than what it represents: an album already on the chart building momentum rather than fading after its opening month, at a moment when the Albums table has otherwise been dominated by projects from outside East Africa.

It's an early data point in a pattern worth watching — whether regional albums can sustain and grow their position over multiple months, the way Iyanii & Dufla's "Donjo Maber" did on the Singles side.
news.author: Data & Analytics Desk

news.title: Gunna Reclaims Albums #1 as Bien's 'Alusa' Storms Into the Top Three
news.excerpt: 'The Last Wun' returns to #1 on Ngoma's Albums chart two months after being dethroned, while Bien's 'Alusa Why Are You Topless?' jumps four places to #2 — Kenya's first top-three album.
news.body:
Gunna's "The Last Wun" is back on top, climbing two places to reclaim #1 on Ngoma's Albums chart with 1,588 points — the first time a former #1 has returned to the summit.

The bigger move belongs to Bien: "Alusa Why Are You Topless?" jumps four places to #2 with 1,486 points, the strongest single-month climb the Albums chart has recorded and the first Kenyan project to reach the top three.

Cardi B's "AM I THE DRAMA? (ErrTime Edition)" drops two spots to #3 (1,427 points), completing a top three that, for the first time, includes an East African title.
news.author: Ngoma Charts Newsroom

news.title: Mbosso's 'Pawa' Ends 'Donjo Maber's Two-Month Reign at #1
news.excerpt: Mbosso's 'Pawa' rises to #1 on Ngoma Charts' November Singles chart, dethroning Iyanii & Dufla's 'Donjo Maber' after two months on top, as Ayra Starr & Rema's 'Who's Dat Girl' debuts at #3.
news.body:
The chart has its first true changeover: Mbosso's "Pawa" climbs one spot to #1 with 2,038 points, ending "Donjo Maber's" two-month hold on the top spot. Iyanii & Dufla's song slides to #2 with 1,859 points — still inside the top two, but no longer leading.

Nigeria's Ayra Starr & Rema debut at #3 with "Who's Dat Girl" (1,692 points), the highest new entry the chart has seen so far. Okello Max's "Taya" and Toxic Lyrikali & Countree Hype's "Backbencher" each slip one place, to #4 and #5 respectively, as the table shuffles for the first time since launch.

With the top spot now changing hands for the first time, Ngoma Charts' Singles chart has its first real storyline: can "Pawa" build a run of its own, or is turnover the new normal?
news.author: Ngoma Charts Newsroom

news.title: Two Months, One Spot: Inside 'Donjo Maber's Run at #1
news.excerpt: Iyanii & Dufla's 'Donjo Maber' has now spent two consecutive months atop the Ngoma Charts Singles chart — the longest run yet on a table that's only two months old.
news.body:
No song has spent longer at #1 on Ngoma Charts than Iyanii & Dufla's "Donjo Maber." It opened the chart's very first month on top and has yet to be moved, closing October still at #1 with 2,157 points.

The pairing of Iyanii, a Kenyan artist, and Dufla gave the chart's debut month its signature song, and its staying power through a second month suggests more than a launch-week spike — sustained six-platform performance across two full monthly cycles.

Every #1 record on Ngoma Charts will eventually be broken by a longer one. For now, "Donjo Maber's" two-month run is the number to beat.
news.author: Artist Desk

news.title: Cardi B Dethrones Gunna to Open Ngoma's Albums Chart's Second Month
news.excerpt: Cardi B's 'AM I THE DRAMA? (ErrTime Edition)' debuts at #1 on Ngoma Charts' Albums table, pushing September's chart-topper Gunna down to #3 as Young Thug's 'UY SCUTI' enters at #2.
news.body:
Ngoma's Albums chart has its first change at the top: Cardi B's "AM I THE DRAMA? (ErrTime Edition)" debuts at #1 with 2,058 points, unseating Gunna's "The Last Wun" after a single month in charge.

Young Thug's "UY SCUTI" enters directly at #2 with 1,681 points, while "The Last Wun" slides two places to #3 (1,531 points) — still a Top 3 fixture, but no longer on top.

It's the first reminder that nothing on Ngoma Charts holds its position by default. Next month will show whether Cardi B can do what Gunna couldn't: defend the #1 spot.
news.author: Ngoma Charts Newsroom

news.title: Donjo Maber Holds #1 for a Second Month as Ngoma Charts' October Table Sets
news.excerpt: Iyanii & Dufla's 'Donjo Maber' repeats at #1 in Ngoma Charts' second Singles chart, while Toxic Lyrikali & Countree Hype's 'Backbencher' and Joshua Baraka & JAE5's 'Wrong Places' both climb into the top five.
news.body:
Two months in, and Iyanii & Dufla's "Donjo Maber" is still on top, holding #1 with 2,157 points as Ngoma Charts' second Singles chart closes. Mbosso's "Pawa" holds at #2 (2,112 points) and Okello Max's "Taya" stays at #3 (1,820 points) — the entire top three repeats from September, unchanged.

Movement picks up just below: Toxic Lyrikali & Countree Hype's "Backbencher" climbs one spot to #4 (1,770 points), and Joshua Baraka & JAE5's "Wrong Places" rises from #6 to #5 (1,659 points), its first appearance in the chart's published top five.

With the top three now locked in for a second straight month, the question heading into November is whether anything can break the early hierarchy — or whether "Donjo Maber" extends its reign to three.
news.author: Ngoma Charts Newsroom

news.title: First Chart Week: What the Data Shows About Ngoma's Opening Table
news.excerpt: A country-by-country look at Ngoma Charts' first Singles Top 50: Tanzania leads with 17 entries, Kenya follows with 13, and eight other countries share the remaining third of the table.
news.body:
With the first Singles Top 50 complete, the data shows a table led by East Africa: Tanzania placed 17 songs in the opening Top 50, the most of any country, with Kenya close behind at 13. Together, the two countries account for 30 of the chart's first 50 positions.

Nigeria placed six entries in the debut table, South Africa four, and the United States and Jamaica two apiece, with Ghana, Uganda, Canada, Rwanda, and Chile each landing a single entry.

It's an early snapshot, not a trend — but it sets a baseline. Every month from here, this breakdown will move, and Ngoma Charts will be tracking exactly how.
news.author: Data & Analytics Desk

news.title: Gunna's 'The Last Wun' Debuts Atop Ngoma's First Albums Chart
news.excerpt: Gunna opens Ngoma Charts' first Albums chart at #1 with 'The Last Wun,' edging out Burna Boy's 'No Sign of Weakness' and Omah Lay's 'Boy Alone (Deluxe Edition)' in a top three led entirely by acts outside East Africa.
news.body:
Ngoma Charts' first Albums chart opens with Gunna's "The Last Wun" at #1, posting 1,563 combined points across six platforms in its debut month.

Burna Boy's "No Sign of Weakness" follows closely at #2 with 1,445 points, with Omah Lay's deluxe edition of "Boy Alone" completing the top three at 1,439 points. All three of the chart's opening leaders arrive from outside East Africa, a reminder that the Albums chart, like the Singles chart, ranks releases on a single global table regardless of origin.

Whether a regional favourite can break into that top tier will be one of the first storylines to watch as the Albums chart enters its second month.
news.author: Ngoma Charts Newsroom

news.title: Iyanii & Dufla's 'Donjo Maber' Claims Ngoma Charts' Very First #1
news.excerpt: Ngoma Charts' inaugural Singles chart is topped by Iyanii & Dufla's "Donjo Maber," opening the platform's first monthly cycle with 2,309 combined points across all six platforms.
news.body:
The first Ngoma Charts Singles chart is in the books, and Iyanii & Dufla's "Donjo Maber" takes the inaugural #1 with 2,309 combined points, arriving at the top in its first four weeks of eligibility.

Mbosso's "Pawa" opens at #2 with 2,203 points, giving Tanzania an immediate foothold at the top of the table. Kenya doubles up at #3 through Okello Max's "Taya" (1,957 points), while Marioo & Bien's cross-border "Nairobi" rounds out the top four at 1,879 points.

Toxic Lyrikali & Countree Hype's "Backbencher" completes the opening top five at #5 with 1,786 points, giving Kenya three of the first chart's top five positions.

With no history to compare against, every entry on this first chart is technically a new entry — but the real test starts next month, when "Donjo Maber" defends the #1 spot it just claimed.
news.author: Ngoma Charts Newsroom

news.title: How a Ngoma Charts Ranking Actually Gets Built
news.excerpt: Before the first chart closes, here's exactly what goes into a rank: six platforms, combined points, and a monthly reset that rewards sustained performance over one-off spikes.
news.body:
Every Ngoma Charts rank starts with raw performance data pulled from six platforms. Streams, plays, and engagement are converted into points for each release, then summed into a single combined score for the month.

That combined score, not any single platform's number, decides the rank. A release that performs modestly everywhere can outrank one that spikes on a single platform, because the chart rewards reach across the full six-platform footprint rather than a single dominant source.

Ranks reset with fresh data every month, but history isn't discarded — each entry carries its previous rank, peak rank, and total weeks on the chart, so movement (new, up, down, holding) is visible at a glance. A release that stays in the Top 50 for several months in a row builds a weeks-on-chart total that becomes its own kind of achievement.

Points also feed a separate certification system: cross a threshold and a release earns Gold; go further and it earns Platinum. More on that as certifications begin rolling out.
news.author: Ngoma Charts Editorial

news.title: Ngoma Charts Goes Live: A New Home for East Africa's Music Data
news.excerpt: Ngoma Charts launches today, tracking combined streaming and airplay performance across six platforms for singles and albums, with East Africa at its core and the rest of the world welcome to compete.
news.body:
Ngoma Charts is officially live. Starting this week, the platform begins publishing monthly Singles and Albums charts built from combined performance across six platforms, alongside regional breakdowns for Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, and beyond.

Every release enters the same combined ranking regardless of where it comes from — a song from Nairobi competes on the same table as one from Lagos, Kingston, or Atlanta. Points are recalculated each month from six-platform performance data, and rankings move as songs rise, fall, or hold.

The first monthly cycle is already underway, with results due when September closes at the end of the month. From here, Ngoma Charts will track not just who's on top, but how they got there — new entries, re-entries, milestones, and the certifications that follow when a release crosses a points threshold.

Welcome to Ngoma Charts.
